A1.justification: Despite different titles, both PDFs describe the same RCP/RCPD research and share identifiable methods and results. The complete text, figures, tables and equations support comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, reasoning-truncation experiments, feature-importance analysis and stopping-rule comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds semantic-convergence measurements, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B evaluations and intermediate-answer intervention results.

M1.justification: The four online rank-history stopping conditions remain unchanged in Appendix C. Offline supervision is revised in its specification: v1 describes model-assisted manual RCP annotation, whereas v2 Section 5.1 specifies controlled truncation and semantic probes using the joint convergence criterion. This does not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Math500 rule mining and AIME24, AIME25 and GPQA-D evaluation remain. Appendix F adds a distinct corrupted-reasoning scenario by manually changing intermediate answers before continuing generation; the new semantic analyses otherwise use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds S-GRPO comparisons for Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B on AIME24 and GPQA-D, explicitly importing results from its paper. Full, BF, No-Think, DEER and the top-5 stopping comparator are retained. Qwen3-32B comparisons move to Table 4 rather than being removed.

E3.justification: v2 introduces protocols for embedding sampled continuations, PCA projection, Gaussian/KL convergence measurement and controlled intermediate-answer interventions. It adds DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B evaluation and the RPCR metric, using Qwen3-8B's No-Think reference for that model. These substantially expand evaluation design beyond v1's length and accuracy analyses.

E4.justification: New analyses test semantic convergence and post-RCP answer anchoring through trajectory measurements and counterfactual injections (Sections 3–4; Appendices D–F). The BF sweep and top-5 ablation are retained. v1's CatBoost feature-importance analysis and manually identified RCP compression estimates disappear.

E5.justification: v1 supplies point estimates without explicit repeated-run counts or uncertainty regions. v2 introduces independently sampled continuations, covariance-based nominal 95% semantic ellipses, and 64 independent trials per injection condition. These characterize semantic dispersion and intervention outcomes; benchmark accuracy still lacks uncertainty estimates, and the semantic continuation count remains unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek, S-GRPO, RPCR, semantic-containment and injection results, including adoption of injected answers in 49/64 and 51/64 trials. No-Think values change, including Qwen3-8B GPQA-D accuracy from 50.00 to 38.13. Shared task-level Qwen RCPD scores remain unchanged, while aggregate corrections include Qwen3-14B accuracy from 69.13 to 69.80. Table 2 loses token results.

T1.justification: v1's stages and RCP are described verbally. v2 introduces Gaussian semantic distributions, a KL convergence residual, quantitative pre/post-RCP conditions and a joint minimum-step RCP definition (Equations 3–8), plus the ellipse assumptions and construction in Appendix D. The stopping-rule equations themselves restate existing rules.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from a three-stage length-based framework to two regimes characterized jointly by length and semantic dynamics. v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion elevate semantic convergence and post-RCP redundancy into the principal explanation of overthinking, while retaining the early-exit efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving semantic stationarity, dynamic equilibrium and confirmation bias. Its limitations section explicitly restricts demonstrated applicability to the tested reasoning-model families and identifies closed models, tool-augmented agents and multimodal models as untested, qualifying v1's broader language about universality.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents NLTK segmentation, Qwen3 embeddings, official chat templates, the 32,768-token cap, token accounting and retrospective BF calibration. It promises code/data upon acceptance without establishing an available release. Explicit TopK/MinP and CatBoost details disappear; numerical semantic sampling, PCA and threshold settings remain incomplete.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around semantic trajectories and representation geometry, citing Cho et al. and Li et al., and adds newer early-exit work such as Sun et al. and Pu et al. It distinguishes auxiliary-component approaches from intrinsic-signal early exit and explicitly aligns RCPD with DEER. Several earlier references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and explanatory narrative are extensively rewritten. The earlier Motivation/Method structure becomes separate length-dynamics, semantic-dynamics, RCP and online-detection sections. Related work moves later, supporting material moves into appendices, and limitations and disclosure sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the overview and stage diagrams, adds semantic trajectories, convergence plots, highlighted observations and case tables, and restructures results tables around RPCR. Qwen3-32B results and the unchanged BF sweep move to appendices. The stopping ablation loses its token column. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more explicit RCP formulation, additional semantic and intervention evidence, corrected aggregate results and clearer applicability limits. These support a limited net improvement. Gains are constrained by unspecified semantic-analysis settings, removal of ablation token results, and inconsistencies in the claimed BF budget matching: Qwen3-8B/AIME25 still reports 11,772 BF tokens versus 10,067 for RCPD.
